critical_issues.suggestion: Remove await self.session.refresh(campaign) and let the router's dependency own the commit/refresh lifecycle.

critical_issues.msg: flush() + refresh() pattern also at line 77 (update_campaign) and line 155 (record_event) — same violation repeats 3 times.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove all three await self.session.refresh() calls. Flush only when auto-generated IDs or IntegrityError surfacing is needed.

critical_issues.msg: tenant_id defaults to 0 — allows cross-tenant access if caller omits the parameter (rule 6: every SQL query must filter by tenant_id).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove default: def create_campaign(..., tenant_id: int, ...) so the caller is forced to provide it.

critical_issues.msg: get_campaign and other methods default tenant_id to 0 — same unsafe default propagates across all methods.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove all tenant_id default values across all method signatures.

critical_issues.msg: update_campaign uses setattr on any attribute present in kwargs with no allowlist — callers can set internal or unintended fields.
critical_issues.suggestion: Maintain an explicit allowlist: ALLOWED_UPDATE_FIELDS = {'name', 'status', 'subject', ...} and only set attributes in that set.

critical_issues.msg: delete_campaign has no tenant_id filter — delete is not gated by tenant_id, allowing cross-tenant deletion if tenant_id is omitted or defaulted.
critical_issues.suggestion: delete_campaign already calls get_campaign which filters by tenant_id, so the fetch is safe; however the explicit session.delete call is fine. No change needed if tenant_id default is removed from method signature.

critical_issues.msg: _seed_user is called once per test but the generated suffix is deterministic within a test — subsequent calls within the same test generate the same UUID suffix, risking unique-constraint violation on username/email.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use a counter or pass an incrementing index to uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] so each call in the same test produces a unique suffix: suffix = f'{base}_{call_count}' or pass uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] from the outer test scope.

critical_issues.msg: test_pagination_params asserts body['data']['page'] == 2 and body['data']['page_size'] == 5 — the router's list response only returns {items, total} and does not include 'page' or 'page_size' in the data dict, so this assertion will KeyError at runtime.
critical_issues.suggestion: Either add pagination metadata to the router response (router should return page/page_size in data) or remove these assertions; verify against the actual router implementation.

suggestions.msg: Implementation plan is well-structured; no code to review.
Clean aggregation of all feature routers with proper exports; no issues.
PUT and PATCH endpoints are functionally identical (same kwargs filtering and same service call) — code duplication violates DRY.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove update_campaign_put; merge both methods into a single @router.put/@router.patch or have PATCH call PUT with identical body, or introduce a shared internal helper.

suggestions.msg: CampaignCreate.status field description lists 'scheduled' but the type is `str` with no enum validation — invalid status values will only fail at the service layer, not at the API boundary.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a Pydantic validator or literal union type to CampaignCreate.status to reject invalid values early with a 422 response.

suggestions.msg: CampaignPaginationQuery is defined but never used — page/page_size/status are declared as Query params directly in the handler, making the class dead code.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove CampaignPaginationQuery or use it as the base class for the query parameters.

suggestions.msg: No OpenAPI operation IDs are set — Swagger/docs can become ambiguous with many endpoints.
suggestions.suggestion: Add operation_id to each endpoint, e.g. operation_id="list_campaigns", to keep the OpenAPI spec clean and tooling-friendly.

suggestions.msg: Router registration is correct, exception handlers are comprehensive, lifespan is properly structured; no issues.
CampaignEvent lacks to_dict/from_dict methods unlike Campaign — inconsistent interface.
suggestions.suggestion: Add to_dict() and from_dict() to CampaignEvent for symmetry with Campaign.

suggestions.msg: target_audience is stored as raw SQL-like string with no parameterized validation — if this expression is built from user input, SQL injection risk exists.
suggestions.suggestion: Validate target_audience as a safe tag/segment reference rather than raw SQL; do not execute it directly.

suggestions.msg: _enum_val is defined in the service but is identical to the same-named function nested in Campaign.to_dict — duplication that can drift.
suggestions.suggestion: Import and reuse the model's _enum_val or move it to a shared utils module.

suggestions.msg: get_campaign_stats divides campaign.open_count / sent — if sent_count is 0 the guard handles it, but if open_count or click_count are None (nullable DB column), a TypeError would occur.
suggestions.suggestion: Use getattr(campaign, 'open_count', 0) or ensure columns are NOT NULL with a server default.

suggestions.msg: test_list_pagination creates 3 campaigns with names 'Page Test {i} {suffix}' — if the same test file runs multiple tests in sequence on the same DB, leftover data causes total >= 3 to be unreliable.
suggestions.suggestion: The db_schema fixture truncates tables between tests via TRUNCATE CASCADE, so this is safe; no change needed given the fixture setup.

suggestions.msg: _seed_user is an async method defined inside the test class — it could be shared as a module-level helper or use the existing test fixtures pattern.
suggestions.suggestion: Extract to a pytest fixture or module-level helper to reduce duplication across test methods.

suggestions.msg: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] returns a bare MagicMock() — the mock has no async __aenter__/__aexit__, which means if the router ever uses the session's transaction context (e.g., __aenter__) the mock will return None and the test will fail silently.
suggestions.suggestion: Use AsyncMock() or configure the mock to return a proper async context manager: MagicMock(__aenter__=AsyncMock(return_value=MagicMock()), __aexit__=AsyncMock(return_value=None))
